speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: It is not just a facility where we import most of our daily necessities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Our investments in the port over the years have paid off.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Today, Singapore is the world’s largest transhipment hub, recognised for our reliability and efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We have won the Asian Freight, Logistics and Supply Chain Best Seaport (Asia) award for 29 years in a row.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Given the strategic interests at stake, it is important for the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) to have oversight on changes in substantive equity control in licensees that provide essential services at the port.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The intent is not to control the day-to-day operations of these licensees, but rather to require MPA’s approval to be sought for transactions in equity interest that would materially change the equity control of these licensees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This Bill thus seeks to amend the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore Act to give effect to this proposal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Clause 8 gives MPA the powers to reject an acquisition or disposal of equity interest in key designated entities if it deems the acquisition or disposal to be detrimental to the interests of the port.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: These designated entities include designated public licensees, designated business trusts and designated equity interest holders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Under the Bill, designated entities will be subject to three key controls relating to changes in equity interest in the entities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Bill will amend the MPA Act in two other areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Today, vessels operating in the reservoirs of Singapore are licensed by the Public Utilities Board (PUB), taking into account MPA’s technical inputs on safety requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: As the authority for the safety standards of marine vessels, MPA should set the safety standards for vessels operating in reservoirs and other inland waterways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Clauses 4 and 9 of the Bill grant MPA the power to set such safety standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: MPA will work with PUB to develop and implement these safety standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This will enhance the overall safety in reservoirs and inland waterways for all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This will provide greater flexibility for the Minister to appoint more members as he deems appropriate to bring in the relevant experience and expertise as needed onto the MPA Board.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The new part 12(a) which includes section 86 A to L is being introduced, notwithstanding the existing provisions in, say, sections 81 to 89.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The existing sections 81 to 89 already provide guidelines on conditions to be set upon grants of public licences.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, section 81A provides that conditions in the public licence may contain control and restriction directly or indirectly on the creation, holding or disposal of shares in the public licensee.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There are various remedial directions which can be given by the authority when there is a breach.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is a very detailed section on what it means to be an associate or subsidiary for purposes of determining direct or indirect control of a designated entity.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, I would appreciate if the Senior Minister of State can explain a little further as to why such onerous requirements from the licensees are in this Bill.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If so, I would appreciate if the Senior Minister of State can share with the House the details of any such past incident.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Under the existing provisions, if there is any contravention of the conditions for a public licence, the authority may cancel or suspense his licence or require the payment of a fine as he thinks fit.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I am not in favour of any fine that can be decided at the complete discretion of the authority, which is the existing law.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I would be grateful if the Senior Minister of State could explain the need for such heavy punishments.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Such designation may only be made by the authority after consultation with the Minister if he considers that it is necessary in the public interest.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: One, I would like to know why there is a provision for designated public licensee, business trust and equity interest holders.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Two, what qualifies for, as I quote from the Bill "necessary in the public interest"?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will the Senior Minister of State please elaborate on the considerations which will be taken into account when the authority is making such designations?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will the Senior Minister of State be able to share any examples?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Next, why are the considerations not set out expressly in section 86D?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Next, Mr Speaker, the proposed section 86E requires that if a person becomes a 5% controller of a designated public licensee holder, designated public trust or designated equity interest holder as a result of an increase in the holding of equity interest or in the voting power controlled by that person or any associate of that person, he must notify the authority in writing.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Again, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State what is the rationale for this.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Would the new provisions in section 86F requiring persons to seek prior approval before becoming a 25%, 50% or 75% controller of designated entities be sufficient?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Next, I move on to the regulation of inland craft.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Permits for use on inland waterways and reservoir remain under the authority of PUB, and rightly so.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is a change in the right direction as MPA is the more appropriate authority for water borne vessels and craft.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Operationally, how will MPA ensure that, on the ground, all vessels or inland crafts operate safely and in compliance with all regulations governing safe operation and navigation in the reservoirs and inland waterways?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will PUB still be working with the MPA in this area?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If so, what will be their role on the ground?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They are our iconic tourist spots, venues for sports and our sources of drinking water.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Hence, I believe any amendments to the MPA Act must augment the way the MPA governs and administers matters in relation to the responsible and safe use of our precious assets.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While I congratulate the Ministry on this well-drafted Bill, I hope to obtain some clarifications.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: First, I agree that the expansion of the functions and duties of the Authority by including the regulation of the operation and safety of inland craft is necessary.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: After all, we wish to ensure that our waterways will be used responsibly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But since possible regulations have not been announced to the public, I wish to seek some clarifications.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: According to Eugene Heng, the Founder and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Waterways Watch Society, “We are currently permitted to operate vessels with four-stroke engines, battery-operated electric vessels, or solar-powered vessels.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We hope this will continue.” Eugene explained that a blanket change to battery-operated or solar-powered vessels would increase costs significantly for smaller operators.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Further, many operators do not have access to the required charging facilities at their jetties.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In view of the cost concerns that operators may face in possible regulations of engines, I hope that extensive consultations will be made with Waterways Watch Society and other non-government organisations (NGOs) and companies, and that any regulations will be done gradually.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If such changes are necessary, I also hope the Ministry will provide some grants to the NGOs to help offset the costs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, as it stands, all powered harbour craft must be installed with either a Harbour Craft Transponder System (HARTS) or Automated Identification System (AIS).

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have also received some feedback from the Waterways Watch Society in relation to this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They have requested that this requirement should be reserved for vessels that are operating in the seas only.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, being precious assets of Singapore, I believe that it is of paramount importance that our waterways remain free from pollution.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Taking a leaf from the European Code for Inland Waterways, Chapter 10 therein provides for the prevention of water and disposal of waste generated on board vessels.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The articles in Chapter 10 make explicit prohibitions on discharging and dumping, collection of waste, and places obligation on the boatmasters and crew members to exercise care to avoid polluting waterways and to restrict the amount of waste generated on board the vessels.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that something similar to Chapter 10 of the European Code exists in Parts 2 and 3 of the Prevention of Pollution of the Sea Act.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, it appears that there is no requirement in the MPA Act and the Prevention of Pollution of the Sea Act, for the boatmaster and crew members to exercise the said care.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In view of this, can the Ministry consider making such regulations or amendments in the future?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am supportive of placing such obligations on such users of the waterways who are likely sources of pollution, in order to protect our waterways for the benefit of the environment and other stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Hence, I hope that the Ministry will seriously consider making such regulations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I trust that the amendments have been drafted with the best intentions to ensure that our waters will be used responsibly and safely.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope that extensive consultations with the stakeholders will be done before any regulations take effect and that changes, again, will be gradual.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: With that, I stand in support of this Bill.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As I mentioned in my speech earlier, our port is a national strategic infrastructure.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The Government has made significant investments in developing the port.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And we will make even greater investments, especially in building up Tuas Terminal, over the next few decades.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Tan also asked how MPA decided on the 5%, 25% and 50% acquisition thresholds, and the 50% and 75% disposal thresholds.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Under the Companies Act, a 5% shareholder is considered a substantial shareholder.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Although a 5% shareholder typically does not have significant powers to drastically influence the direction of a company, it is still important for MPA to be informed of any new substantial shareholders of its designated public licensees.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Shareholders with 25% or 50% interest, however, wield significant voting power in a company’s decisions.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These are the reasons why MPA should have some regulatory oversight on shareholders seeking to reach 25% and 50% of the equity interest respectively.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: On the other hand, a shareholder will lose its ability to control special resolutions if its equity interest falls below 75%.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It will lose its ability to control ordinary resolutions if its equity interest falls below 50%.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As these are important corporate decisions that could impact the overall direction of the company, MPA should maintain oversight on whether it is in our national interest for any incumbent shareholders to relinquish such voting powers.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The acquisition controls enable MPA to have oversight of single persons becoming a new major shareholder of a designated entity.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The disposal controls grant MPA oversight of existing shareholders from selling interest in a designated entity, whether to a single or multiple persons.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Dennis Tan also asked whether the thresholds set are too onerous.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But, in fact, we are at most on par with those with similar legislation for other sectors, and they are not more stringent.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Currently, vessels operating in reservoirs of Singapore are regulated and given permits to use the inland water bodies by PUB.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: MPA is the authority for safety standards for marine vessels and thus has the relevant expertise and experience and is in a good position to assume the responsibility for setting the safety standards for vessels operating in reservoirs and inland waterways.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This will further enhance safety of navigation in these water bodies.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: PUB will continue to be the authority to issue permits to vessels for use in reservoirs and inland waterways for the purpose of water quality control, protection of reservoir infrastructure, controlling the types of activities in these water bodies and preventing social disamenities.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Louis Ng asked whether the Bill will require inland vessels currently fitted with four-stroke engines to switch to other engine types, such as battery or solar-powered ones.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: PUB, which remains as the overall manager of reservoirs and inland waterways, will continue to allow vessels with four-stroke engines to operate in these water bodies.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked if MPA intends to require inland water vessels to be fitted with AIS transponders.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I agree with Mr Louis Ng that there is no need at this point to require inland water vessels to install such equipment.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I share Mr Louis Ng’s concern for the environment.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: PUB already has existing measures to safeguard against the pollution of our waterways from vessels.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For instance, PUB’s regulations prohibit inland water vessels from discharging wastewater and other pollutants.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These measures have been effective in keeping our reservoirs and waterways clean.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Hence, there is no need to amend the MPA Act or the Prevention of Pollution of the Sea Act to preserve the pristine conditions of our water bodies.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Lastly, on the question by Mr Dennis Tan about why we are legislating the equity interest holders as well as the business trust.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In many instances, it is the parent company that would have the power to control key decisions of the licensee.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I think he may have missed out my question.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Regarding section 86D, designating public licensee, my questions include (a) I would like to know why there is a provision for a designated public licensee and what would qualify as necessary in the public interest.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Will the Senior Minister of State be able to share any examples and, if not, why are the considerations not set out in the section itself?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Would the consideration be set out in any subsidiary legislation?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: MPA will have to decide which are the public licensees that are to be designated.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At this point in time, we are looking at the port operators, the terminals.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But, of course, if we deem that there are certain other areas within the maritime sector that require the designation of being the designated public licensee, we will put in measures to ensure that as well.
